questions.answer: Observation describes recorded behaviour; interpretation proposes its meaning or cause.
questions.feedback: Rewrite a personal judgement as an observation.

questions.prompt: Why include strengths as well as gaps?
questions.answer: The review should preserve effective actions while correcting specific weaknesses.

questions.prompt: Do debrief studies guarantee a fixed improvement?
questions.answer: No; average effects depend on contexts and implementation.
questions.feedback: Do not promise a percentage gain.

questions.prompt: What should follow a useful debrief?
questions.answer: A specific, feasible change tested against a comparable task criterion.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer, formative only; use specific feedback and delayed retest.
scoring.practice: Conducts an evidence-based, respectful debrief that identifies a testable improvement without making a personal or clinical judgement.
scoring.transfer: Complete the presentation rehearsal capstone with a task-pressure map, two low-stakes rounds, process/outcome scorecard and structured debrief. Include one revised attempt on a novel fictional case and a clear limit on what the evidence establishes.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; never average away missing or safety-critical evidence. Quizzes cannot certify competence.
